title: Bundle Install Receipt (.harness/.bundle-manifest.json)
description: What an install run did to a project, written by install.ps1 / install.sh. `version` and `content_hash` name the bundle the run was driven by; they are NOT a claim that every file landed. `status` and each file's `state` are: a receipt that says only 'version X' while files were skipped or left in conflict is a false report. Receipts written before per-file states existed carry no `status`/`state`/`counts`; readers treat their files as installed. Governs the assistant-plane install process, never the product runtime.

version.description: Version of the bundle this run was driven by.

content_hash.description: Content hash of that bundle artifact.

status.description: complete = no file was left in conflict or skipped. partial = at least one was; see `files[].state`. 'kept' alone does not make a receipt partial: the project chose that file.

preserve.description: Paths this install treated as project-owned.

sha256.description: Hash of the bytes the bundle shipped for this path. 'unknown' for an empty file: the hash of nothing is a real hash and would make any empty file look verified.

installed_sha256.description: For state=installed: hash of the file this run left on disk (re-stamped after scaffolding). For every other state: the baseline CARRIED from the previous receipt, 'unknown' when there was none. Never the hash of a hand-edited or conflicted file.

state.description: installed = on disk is what this run put there (written, merged, or already identical). kept = project-owned, or hand-edited while the bundle did not change it. conflict = hand-edited AND changed by the bundle: yours kept, shipped copy beside it as <file>.new. skipped = exists and no --force.
